skill.name: project-creator
skill.description: Creates CCGG Business Operations project workspaces with required templates, parent-system integration, dependency tracking, operations logging, and validation guidance.
skill.summary: Guides creation of CCGG project workspaces with templates, dependency tracking, parent-system integration, and validation checks.
skill.author: Daron Vener

security_audit.summary: All 120 static detections were adjudicated as false positives caused by Markdown code spans, fixed CCGG paths, repository metadata, or benign validation-script markers. No prompt injection, secret access, outbound network behavior, obfuscated code, or malicious command execution was found. The skill still performs project-scaffolding work and should document its expected workspace boundary.

remediation.suggestion: Document that the skill is only for the CCGG Business Operations root and require confirmation before writing outside the new project folder.

remediation.issue: The legacy Bash validator does not enforce the documented hyphen-case project name format.
remediation.suggestion: Add a strict project-name regex before constructing PROJECT_PATH or INDEX_PATH.

remediation.issue: Manual shell logging examples can be copied into terminals.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the Python validator or an agent file-write step for operations log updates, avoiding shell examples for user-provided text.

content.value_statement: Project setup often misses shared operations, index, and logging requirements. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured CCGG project creation with templates and validation checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides intake for simple and complex CCGG projects.
Provides templates for CLAUDE.md, README.md, phase trackers, and project index entries.
Documents parent-system integration for index sync, operations logging, strategic alignment, and related project search.
Captures dependency metadata for upstream, downstream, and related parallel projects.
Includes Python and legacy Bash validation guidance for required project mechanisms.
Defines completion reporting steps after project creation.
limitations: The workflow is tailored to CCGG Business Operations folder conventions.
The current creation workflow is mostly manual; the full creation script is not implemented.
Validation checks required sections and files, not the business quality of generated content.
The skill expects users to provide accurate project scope, dependencies, and strategic context.

use_cases.title: Standardize Incubator Setup
use_cases.description: Create consistent folder structure, project guidance, README content, index entries, and validation steps for a new incubator project.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Phase Work
use_cases.description: Detect projects that need validation phases and prepare phase tracker guidance with milestones, transition triggers, and completion criteria.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Connected Projects
use_cases.description: Set up complex projects with dependency metadata, Coordination Hub guidance, and links to related project outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new CCGG project named [project-name]. Ask the required intake questions, then prepare the standard project files and validation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Phased Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CCGG project for [goal]. Detect whether phases are needed, propose phase names and durations, then prepare the phase tracker content.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Coordinated Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a complex CCGG project that depends on [upstream projects] and supports [downstream projects]. Include dependency metadata and Coordination Hub guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the project named [project-name] against Project Creator requirements. Report missing templates, index entries, parent integration sections, logs, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create a simple project for member retention email sequences.
output_examples.output: The assistant gathers purpose, deliverables, avatars, and dependency status, then prepares standard project guidance, README content, index content, log guidance, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create a complex project for a new offers and pricing strategy.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies upstream and downstream projects, recommends complex setup, prepares dependency metadata, adds Coordination Hub guidance, and includes cross-project validation steps.

output_examples.input: Check whether the project setup is complete.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares the project against required sections, index entry expectations, operations log requirements, template replacement status, and validation outcomes.

best_practices: Confirm the project name, purpose, dependencies, deliverables, and avatars before creating files.
Use the Python validation script when available, because it is the recommended cross-platform option.
Review generated parent-system integration paths before writing outside the new project folder.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill outside the CCGG Business Operations structure without adjusting paths.
Do not skip dependency capture, even when the project appears simple.
Do not mark validation complete while template placeholders remain unreplaced.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides creation of CCGG project files, index entries, phase trackers, dependency notes, operations log guidance, and validation steps.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create complex projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for projects with dependencies, coordination needs, and downstream handoffs.

faq.question: Does it include automated creation scripts?
faq.answer: Not fully. The skill documents a planned creation script and currently relies on templates plus manual variable replacement.

faq.question: How does validation work?
faq.answer: The included validators check required files, parent-system sections, index entries, operations log entries, and remaining template placeholders.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is best for teams using the CCGG Business Operations structure and needing repeatable project setup.
